items.difficulty_reason: For a continuous homomorphism of linearly topologized rings that is taut with weakly pre-admissible source, the lemma asserts that the target is weakly pre-admissible (statement lines 1421-1426). The proof produces a weak ideal of definition of the target directly: a weak ideal of definition I of A is chosen, tautness gives that the closure J of IB is open, the earlier lemma on topologically nilpotent elements gives that J consists of topologically nilpotent elements, and therefore J is a weak ideal of definition of B (proof lines 1428-1433). The level is H2: the two ingredients (openness from tautness and the nilpotent-element description of the closure) are combined in a single displayed move, nothing is omitted.
